senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. עָרָה I)to lay bare, strip, denude; to make lonely. Pesik. ʿĂniya, p. 134ᵇ (expl. סערה, Is. LIV, 11) מערערתא שעִרְעֲרוּהָ וכ׳ ‘the stripped’ (or lonely) one whom the nations have denuded (with ref. to ערו, Ps. CXXXVII, 7); Yalk. s. 339 שעיר ערוה (read: שעִירְעֲרוּהָ).
units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 708:2">Yalk. Num. 708</cite> (play on <he>המים המאררים למרים</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 5:24">Num. V, 24</cite>) <he>שממררין את הגוף ומְעַרְעֲרִין את העון</he> (not <he>שממרין</he>) because they make the body bitter (sick), and lay the sin bare; <cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 11:1">Sifré Num. 11</cite> <he>ומרעדים את העין</he> (corr. acc.); <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 9:16">Num. R. s. 9</cite> <he>שמאררים את הגוף ומבערין וכ׳</he> (corr. acc.; v., also, <cite ref="B01335"><he>בָּרַר</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 102:4">Midr. Till. to Ps. CII, 18</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="P01419"><he>ערער</he></cite>, <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 102:4">ib.</cite>) <he>זה מנשה שנתע׳ ממעשים טובים</he> (some ed. <he>שערער</he>, corr. acc.; ed. Bub. <he>שחיה ער</he>, read <cite ref="P01423"><he>עַרְעָר</he></cite>) this refers to Manasseh who was bare of good deeds.—V. <cite ref="P01423"><he>עַרְעָר</he></cite>.
